'''''Ligustrum vulgare''''' ('''wild privet''', also sometimes known as '''common privet''' or '''European privet''') is a [[species]] of ''[[Ligustrum]]'' native to central and southern [[Europe]], [[north Africa]] and southwestern [[Asia]], from [[Ireland]] and southwestern [[Sweden]] south to [[Morocco]], and east to [[Poland]] and northwestern [[Iran]].<ref name="fe">Flora Europaea: [http://rbg-web2.rbge.org.uk/cgi-bin/nph-readbtree.pl/feout?FAMILY_XREF=&GENUS_XREF=Ligustrum+&SPECIES_XREF=vulgare&TAXON_NAME_XREF=&RANK= ''Ligustrum vulgare'']</ref><ref>{{PFAF|Ligustrum vulgare}}</ref><ref>{{GRIN | accessdate = 17 December 2017}}</ref><ref name="blamey">Blamey, M. & Grey-Wilson, C. (1989). ''Flora of Britain and Northern Europe''. {{ISBN|0-340-40170-2}}</ref><ref name="bean">Bean, W. J. (1978). ''Trees and Shrubs Hardy in the British Isles'' vol. 2: 576–577. {{ISBN|0-7195-2256-0}}.</ref>

==Description==
[[Image:- Ligustrum vulgare - Berries -.jpg|thumb|Berries]]
It is a [[evergreen|semi-evergreen]] or [[deciduous]] [[shrub]], growing to 3 m (rarely up to 5 m) tall. The stems are stiff, erect, with grey-brown [[Bark (botany)|bark]] spotted with small brown [[lenticel]]s. The [[leaf|leaves]] are borne in decussate opposite pairs, sub-shiny green, narrow oval to lanceolate, 2–6 cm long and 0.5–1.5 cm broad. The [[flower]]s are produced in mid-summer in [[panicle]]s 3–6 cm long, each flower creamy-white, with a tubular base and a four-lobed [[Corolla (flower)|corolla]] ('petals') 4–6 mm diameter.  The flowers produce a strong, pungent fragrance that many people find unpleasant.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ligustrum vulgare (Common Privet) |url=https://www.gardenia.net/plant/ligustrum-vulgare |access-date=2025-05-15 |website=Gardenia |language=en-US}}</ref> The [[fruit]] is a small glossy black [[berry (botany)|berry]] 6–8 mm diameter, containing one to four [[seed]]s. The berries are [[poison]]ous to humans but readily eaten by [[thrush (bird)|thrushes]], which disperse the seeds in their droppings.<ref name=blamey/><ref name=bean/><ref name=fnwe>Flora of Northwest Europe: [http://ip30.eti.uva.nl/BIS/flora.php?selected=beschrijving&menuentry=soorten&id=3568 ''Ligustrum vulgare'']{{dead link|date=December 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

Plants from the warmer parts of the range show a stronger tendency to be fully evergreen; these have sometimes been treated as a separate [[variety (biology)|variety]] ''Ligustrum vulgare'' var. ''italicum'' (Mill.) Vahl,<ref name=bean/> but others do not regard it as distinct.<ref name=fe/>

==Cultivation and uses==
In the [[British Isles]] it is the only [[native plant|native]] privet, common in [[hedge (barrier)|hedge]]rows and woodlands in southern [[England]] and [[Wales]], especially in chalk areas; it is less common in northern England, [[Scotland]], and [[Northern Ireland]], where it only occurs as an escapee from cultivation.<ref name=bean/><ref name="multiple">The [[Reader's Digest]] Field Guide to the Trees and Shrubs of Britain ''p. 52''.</ref><ref name=fni>Flora of Northern Ireland: [http://www.habitas.org.uk/flora/species.asp?item=3951 ''Ligustrum vulgare'']</ref>

The species was used for hedging in [[Elizabethan gardens]] in England, but was superseded by the more reliably evergreen introduction ''[[Ligustrum ovalifolium|L. ovalifolium]]'' from Japan.<ref name="multiple"/>

A number of [[cultivar]]s have been selected, including:<ref name=bean/>
*'Aureum' – yellow leaves.
*'Buxifolium' – small, oval leaves not over 2.5 cm long.
*'Cheyenne' – cold-tolerant clone selected in North America.
*'Chlorocarpum' - berries green.
*'Insulense' – long, narrow leaves 5–11 cm long and 1–2.5 cm broad.
*'Leucocarpum' – berries greenish-white.
*'Lodense' – dense, dwarf shrub (the name is a [[portmanteau]] of 'low' and 'dense').
*'Pyramidale' – fastigiate.
*'Xanthocarpum' – berries yellow.

==Invasiveness==
{{Main|Privet as an invasive plant}}
The species is listed as [[invasive plant|invasive]] as an introduced plant in [[Australia]],<ref>[https://www.environment.gov.au/biodiversity/invasive/weeds/publications/books/pubs/potential.pdf Potential Environmental Weeds in Australia]</ref> [[Canada]],<ref>Canadian Botanical Conservation Network: [http://www.rbg.ca/cbcn/en/projects/invasives/i_shrub2.html Information on Invasive Shrub and Vine Species] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070827055217/http://www.rbg.ca/cbcn/en/projects/invasives/i_shrub2.html |date=2007-08-27 }}</ref> [[New Zealand]],<ref>Protecting and Restoring our Natural Heritage: [http://www.doc.govt.nz/publications/conservation/protecting-and-restoring-our-natural-heritage-a-practical-guide/appendix-one-invasive-weeds/ Appendix one: Invasive weeds] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150128124201/http://www.doc.govt.nz/publications/conservation/protecting-and-restoring-our-natural-heritage-a-practical-guide/appendix-one-invasive-weeds/ |date=2015-01-28 }}</ref> and the [[United States]].<ref>{{cite book |url=http://www.nps.gov/plants/alien/pubs/midatlantic/midatlantic.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061007092003/http://www.nps.gov/plants/alien/pubs/midatlantic/midatlantic.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-date=October 7, 2006 | title=Plant Invaders of Mid-Atlantic Natural Areas, 4th Edition |last1=Swearingen |first1=Jil |last2=Reshetiloff |first2=K. |last3=Slattery |first3=B |last4=Zwicker |first4=S. | year=2010 |publisher=National Park Service and U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service |page=71}}</ref><ref>Invasive species: [http://www.invasive.org/browse/subject.cfm?sub=3036 European privet]</ref> It is also fully naturalised in [[Mexico]]'s highlands<ref>Plantas medicinales. ==Etymology==
''Ligustrum'' means 'binder'. It was named by [[Pliny the Elder|Pliny]] and Virgil.<ref name="gledhill">Gledhill, David (2008). "The Names of Plants". Cambridge University Press. {{ISBN|9780521866453}} (hardback), {{ISBN|9780521685535}} (paperback).  p 237</ref>
